# Zonorah, Media Neuroscience Lab

> Zonorah is an instrument for observing broadcast media, used in academic research, and the Media Neuroscience Lab that offers it to the public by subscription.

Last updated: 2026-11-24

Zonorah is an instrument for observing broadcast media, developed for academic research. The Media Neuroscience Lab that bears its name now offers it to the public by subscription.

## Home

https://zonorah.com/

The name Zonorah designates two things: an instrument that records and counts broadcast media, developed for academic research, and the Media Neuroscience Lab that maintains it. The laboratory supports research by offering the instrument to the public under a subscription model. Work on the brain is carried out separately and draws on the counts the instrument produces.

## How the numbers are made

1. Record. Each station's live signal comes in over the internet. We record it during the hours of its schedule.
2. Transcribe. A speech-recognition program on our own computer turns the audio into text, with a time for every sentence. Then the audio is deleted.
3. Code. The text is searched for the words each study uses, including their variants. Every passage that matches is entered on a fixed form: who speaks, the role of the person or cause, topic, tone, framing, and whether the claim has evidence or is rumour.
4. Report. The public figures are minutes on air per 100 hours recorded. Inside the panel, reports are generated automatically. Each paid plan adds a custom report, designed with the subscriber and delivered as a PDF by email on a schedule the subscriber chooses.

## Method

https://zonorah.com/method/

These limits apply to every published figure.

### Limit 1: Transcription errors

The speech-recognition program mishears names, acronyms and brands. A misheard word is not counted, so figures tend to be low.

Try several spellings of the same name

### Limit 2: Recorded hours only

A station that was not recorded at some hour tells nothing about what it broadcast then. Absence from the recording does not mean it was not said.

The coverage table shows what is recorded

### Limit 3: Music and advertising

Recorded minutes include songs and adverts. A word inside an advert is counted.

### Limit 4: Comparing stations

A music station and a news station cannot be compared directly. Compare stations of the same type, or the same word over time.

### Limit 5: Rounding and hidden figures

Public figures are rounded to multiples of 5 and hidden below 3 minutes. With exact low figures, someone could tell whether a named person was mentioned at a given moment. Totals may not add up exactly.

### Citing: Citing a figure

Cite the permanent link of the comparison and the date it was consulted. Figures change when recordings are added.

Zonorah (2026). Minutes on air per 100 hours recorded. Consulted [date], terms: [terms]. [link to the comparison]

## Research

https://zonorah.com/research/

The laboratory pursues a single objective, the expansion of research on broadcast media. The instrument supplies recordings, transcripts and methods of analysis, and each field described below states what the instrument contributes and what the researcher must add.

### The instrument: Public access by subscription

Zonorah was developed for academic research and has been used for that purpose throughout. Access is now open to researchers, teachers, journalists and organisations, who may subscribe to a plan. The free plan covers one source and one hour of listening per week, with reports generated automatically in the panel. The comparator, the charts, the CSV files and the El Niño index follow rules that are published and fixed, so that any reader can verify them. The assistant answers from the transcripts and quotes short fragments together with their station and time.

Every figure: minutes on air per 100 hours recorded

### Custom report: Designed in working sessions

Each paid plan includes a custom report. Its design is agreed with the subscriber in working sessions, in which the sources, the keywords, the coding rules and the format of the report are defined. Every mention is entered on a fixed form that records, among other fields, risk and urgency, and a PDF is sent by email on the schedule the subscriber selects. The public figures do not reveal who commissioned which report.

Not tied to a country: the client picks the stations and their language. Reports in English, Spanish or Indonesian

### Computational social science: Descriptive and longitudinal study of media content

The instrument produces the recordings, the transcripts, the identification of topics, the longitudinal counts and the classification of narratives. The researcher formulates the hypotheses, validates the classifications against human annotators and applies suitable statistical methods. A descriptive study of media content requires neither a laboratory nor participants, although what the media say does not permit inferences about what a population thinks.

The researcher adds: hypotheses, validation by human annotators and statistics

### Media psychology: Selection of real stimuli for online experiments

The instrument locates broadcast items on one subject that differ in framing, so that the researcher can select and validate stimuli, recruit participants online and measure emotions, risk perception, recall or attitudes. No physical laboratory is required, but an experimental protocol, informed consent, valid instruments and, where applicable, ethical review are. Zonorah supplies stimuli and analysis; by itself it does not measure emotions or mental processes.

The researcher adds: protocol, participants, psychological measures and ethical review

### Computational cognitive neuroscience: Linguistic features of stimuli, joined to existing neural data

The instrument can extract linguistic and narrative features from the original stimuli of an already published neuroimaging dataset, so that their association with brain activity can be studied. The features must come from exactly the stimuli that correspond to the neural recordings: transcripts of broadcasts cannot be linked automatically to the brains of people who watched other material. The work demands knowledge of neuroimaging, temporal alignment and statistics, but not a scanner of one's own.

The researcher adds: external neural data and its temporal alignment with the stimuli

### Foundations: Origin

Zonorah began as an instrument and later became a laboratory of the same name. The laboratory supports research on media by making the instrument publicly available under a subscription model. Its approach follows the computational work of the Media Neuroscience Lab at UC Santa Barbara, which studies, among other subjects, moral narratives in news and entertainment, text mining and large media datasets. Zonorah does not perform brain imaging or experiments with participants; research on the brain is conducted separately and uses these figures.

medianeuroscience.org ↗

## The instrument

https://zonorah.com/data/

How many minutes a word was on air, by station and by day.

### Compare: Comparator

Up to four words at once, grouped by station, day, hour, region or type of station. The search ignores capital letters and accents and includes variants.

The coverage table shows which stations and hours are recorded

### Download: Downloads and charts

Each comparison downloads as a CSV file with the same columns as the table. The same comparison can be embedded in an article as a chart that shows its source.

### Ask: AI assistant

It summarises the transcripts and quotes short fragments with station and time. It does not give names or data of private individuals. Transcripts are automatic, so a summary can contain mistakes.

### Access

Every paid plan starts with a 7-day free trial, once per person. A card is required: it is charged when the trial ends unless you cancel before.

- Free: one source and 1 hour of listening a week, no card. When it runs out, wait 7 days or subscribe.
- Professional: US$ 89 per month at list price, 100 AI questions a day.
- Intensive: US$ 229 per month at list price, 500 AI questions a day.
- Newsroom: US$ 429 per month at list price, 2,000 AI questions a day.

## Privacy

https://zonorah.com/privacy/

No recordings are kept. This page says what is kept about people who sign in. It is a draft pending legal review.

### Recordings: None are kept

The audio is deleted as soon as it has been turned into text. Only the text stays.

### Your account: What is stored if you sign in with Google

Your email and name as Google gives them, the date you joined and the date of your last visit, how many questions you ask each day, and which sector reports you download.

The password is handled by Google. It is not stored here.

### Your questions: They go to an AI service

A question is sent to an AI service (Groq, in the United States) without your email or name. The text of your questions is not kept with your account. Please do not write personal data in a question.

### Payments: Stripe handles the card

Card payments are processed by Stripe. Zonorah never sees or stores your card number. It keeps your Stripe customer reference, your plan, the status of the subscription and its dates, and a card fingerprint, an identifier Stripe assigns that is not the number, to apply the rule of one free trial per card.

Stripe keeps payment records for as long as the law requires.

### Your monitors: Saved with your account

The searches and monitoring requests you save in the platform (keywords, sources, schedules and languages) belong to your account. When you delete the account, the monitors stop and those data are deleted, including the transcripts and reports made for them. The one thing that can stay is a one-way fingerprint of your email, not the email itself, and only while free listening time you already used or a wait for it to come back is still running: it stops deleting and re-creating the account from resetting the free time.

### How long: Until you delete the account

A session lasts 30 days. Your data stays while the account exists. You can delete the account whenever you want, and everything goes: email, name, sessions and question count.

### Your rights: Access, correction, deletion

You can ask for access to your data, for it to be corrected or for it to be deleted by writing to hola@zonorah.com.

### Status: Draft pending legal review

The wording may change after the review. Companies that order studies are covered by their own agreement, not by this page.

## Terms and refunds

https://zonorah.com/terms/

How the service, billing and refunds work. It is a draft pending legal review.

### Service: What Zonorah is

Zonorah listens to public radio, television and streaming broadcasts, turns the audio into text and analyses it. You use it through an account. The transcripts and analyses are tools to help you read the media; they are not legal, medical or financial advice.

### Plans: Free and paid plans

The free plan gives one source and 1 hour of listening a week, with no card. When the hour is used up you wait 7 days for it to come back, or you subscribe. Paid plans are monthly, priced in US dollars, and are listed on the plans page. Every paid plan includes a custom report that we design with you in working sessions.

### Billing: Trial, renewal and cancelling

Paid plans start with a 7-day free trial that needs a card. There is one trial per account and per card. If you do not cancel before the trial ends, the card is charged and the plan renews every month until you cancel. You can cancel at any time from the billing portal; access continues until the end of the period already paid. Payments are handled by Stripe; Zonorah never sees your card number.

### Refunds: When money is returned

Cancelling stops the next charge; it does not return the month already started. If you were charged by mistake, or you cancelled inside the trial and were charged anyway, write to info@zonorah.com within 14 days and the charge will be returned. Where the law of your country gives you a right to a refund, that right applies.

### Use: What you agree not to do

Use Zonorah only to follow public broadcasts. Do not try to get around the free-plan limits with repeated accounts, do not resell access, and do not use the reports to harass or to profile private individuals. We may suspend an account that does.

### Accuracy: Automatic transcripts can be wrong

Speech recognition and AI analysis make mistakes: a name can be misheard, a word missed, a tone misread. Check any quote against the source before you publish or act on it. Zonorah gives no guarantee that every mention is found.

### Changes: Changes and contact

These terms are a draft pending legal review and may change; the date at the foot of the page shows the last update. The governing law and the court that decides disputes will be fixed after that review. Questions: info@zonorah.com.

Contact: hola@zonorah.com
